        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);

                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();

                            <!-- OC Layout Element Conent Template -->
							              <!--normalTemplateStart--><h1 class='oc-page-title '>Council Meetings</h1>

<p>Council holds monthly Ordinary Meetings and Standing Committee Meetings. Minutes from each past meeting are available through the search function below.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">Alternatively, you can view these documents and previous years' minutes by visiting the reception at Council's Moranbah Administration Centre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">T</span>he <em style="color: inherit; font-size: 1em; font-family: inherit;">Local Government Regulation </em><em>2012</em> requires Council to ensure a copy of the minutes of each Council meeting is available for inspection by the public, at a local government's public office and on its website, within 10 days after the end of a meeting; and when the minutes have been confirmed — must be available for purchase at the local government's public office. </p>
<div data-type="0" data-title-level="2" class="oc-wysiwyg-container">
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Attending Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council's Ordinary and Special meetings are open to the public as part of Council's commitment to transparent decision making and engagement with our community.</p>
<p>Ordinary Meetings are held at Isaac's Customer Services Centres on a rotational basis.</p>
<p>Due to the varied sizes of our Council Chambers, the number of public attendees at each meeting is limited. If you wish to attend a council meeting, please arrive early to secure a seat as there is no booking system in place. Once all seating in the chambers is occupied, we are unable to accept additional attendees.</p>
<p>The rules for conducting meetings are dictated by:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-017" target="_blank">Local Government Act 2009</a></em></li>
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2012-0236" target="_blank">Local Government Regulation 2012</a></em></li>
<li><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i> <span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Conduct of Council Meetings Policy<span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a></li>
<li><a href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025_1.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p>Public attendees must not interrupt the conduct of business at council meetings.  If a person interrupts or obstructs the proper conduct of the meeting, the Chairperson of the meeting may ask the person to withdraw from the meeting place.</p>
<p>Recording of council meetings is prohibited unless first approved by the Chairperson of the meeting.</p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Council Meeting Sessions</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The <em>Local Government Regulation 2012</em> allows Council to close meetings to the public in order to discuss particular matters where they consider it necessary.  Council resolutions (decisions) cannot be made while the meeting is closed to the public, the matter can be discussed and the decision made once the meeting is again in open session. </p>
<p>Council meetings may be closed to the public for the following reasons:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the appointment, discipline or dismissal of the Chief Executive Officer</li>
<li>industrial matters affecting employees</li>
<li>the Council’s budget</li>
<li>rating concessions</li>
<li>legal advice obtained by the Council or legal proceedings involving the Council including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the Council</li>
<li>matters that may directly affect the health and safety of an individual or a group of individuals</li>
<li>negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the Council for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the Council</li>
<li>negotiations relating to the taking of land by the Council under the <em>Acquisition of Land Act 1967</em></li>
<li>a matter the Council is required to keep confidential under a law of, or formal arrangement with, the Commonwealth or State</li>
</ul>
<p>When dealing with confidential agenda items, Council will resolve to enter into a closed session which requires all visitors and guests to vacate the Council Chambers until the meeting is again opened by Council resolution.</p>

<h2>Public Participation at Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The community can engage with Council through our meeting processes in the following ways:</p>
<h5>Petitioning Council</h5>
<p>A petition is a formal written request used to lobby a law-making body such as local government. It may request an amendment to general law or the review of an administrative decision. The petition is placed before the law-making body with the object of implementing the particular action or amendment. Petitioning is one of the traditional forms by which people can make requests direct to Council.</p>
<p>Petitions should not be used to request completion of operational works such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>having a water meter repaired</li>
<li>requesting road repairs</li>
</ul>
<h5>Guidelines for Petitions</h5>
<p>All petitions must meet the following requirements to be determined to be a property made petition for consideration by Council:</p>
<ul>
<li>Contain a clear and concise statement identifying the subject matter of the petition and the action sought from Council</li>
<li>Include a statement specifying the range of numbered of pages to the petition and the total number of signatories</li>
<li>Record a brief statement on each page of the subject matter and the action requested</li>
<li>Contain the full printed name, address, phone number and signature of the person lodging the petition, or if acting on behalf of organisation/group, name of organisation/group</li>
<li>List the names, addresses and signatures of those people who support the petition</li>
<li>Be in the English language or accompanied by a translation certified to be a true and correct translation (including contact details of the translator)</li>
<li>Be a standalone document with no letters, affidavits, or other documents attached</li>
<li>Be respectful and not contain any offensive, defamatory, indecent or abusive language or substance or otherwise offend any rule or practice of Council</li>
<li>Be clearly written or printed and be free from erasures or alterations</li>
<li>Meet all stipulations</li>
<li>Not be requests for grants of public money or remission of any duties</li>
</ul>
<p>Petitions that do not meet the criteria listed above will be deemed invalid and will not be received by Council.</p>
<p>This <a href="https://www.isaac.qld.gov.au/downloads/file/3318/petition-to-council-form"></a><a title="Petition_to_Council_Form.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition_to_council_form.pdf" target="_blank" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>sample petition<span class="file-info">(PDF, 57KB)</span></a> may be used as a guide.</p>
<h5>Signing a Petition</h5>
<p>A petition must be signed by a minimum of ten (10) persons aged 18 years or older, clearly stating their name and address. Each person may not sign more than once and each signature must be an original written upon the petition itself and not pasted upon it or otherwise affixed or transferred to it (e.g. scanned, pasted, photocopied, etc.).</p>
<p>Persons signing the petition must only be signing on behalf of themselves and not acting as proxy for another person.</p>
<h5>Addressing and Lodging the Petition</h5>
<p>A person may lodge a petition with the Council by submitting the petition to an Isaac Regional Council Customer Service Centre in person, or by mail addressed to:</p>
<p>Chief Executive Officer<br />
Isaac Regional Council<br />
PO Box 97<br />
Moranbah Qld 4744</p>
<h5>Actioning a Petition</h5>
<p>Once registered the petition will be forwarded to the CEO and the following process will apply.</p>
<p><img alt="Petition Flowchart.JPG" src="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition-flowchart.jpg?w=954&h=593" /></p>
<p>If the petition lodged is not to be tabled, the Council will notify the person lodging the petition within twenty-one (21) days of lodgement, the reasons for it not being tabled.</p>
<p>If the petition is to be tabled, Council will advise the person lodging the petition, the date the petition is to be tabled.</p>
<h5>Deciding a Petition</h5>
<p>Council will decide what action, if any, it will take on the petition after the petition is tabled at its ordinary meeting.</p>
<p>In the minutes of the deciding meeting, Council will record the subject matter of the petition, the number of signatories to the petition, and what action, if any, it will take.</p>
<p>The Council will inform the person who has lodged the petition of Council's decision within twenty-one (21) days of the petition being tabled.</p>
<h5>Petitioning other Levels of Government</h5>
<p>Find out more about petitioning other levels of the Australian government:</p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/e-petitions">Petition to House of Representatives - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Petitions/Senate_Petitions">Petition to Senate - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.parliament.qld.gov.au/Work-of-the-Assembly/Petitions">Petition to Queensland Parliament - State government website</a></p>
<p>Further information on Petitions to Council can be found in the <a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>
<h4>Deputations</h4>
<p>Deputations are where an individual or a small group address Council on issues that are important to them.  The address can be on any topic, it does not need to be in relation to an item on the Meeting agenda.  Deputations from the public are welcome at Council's Ordinary Meetings.  Deputations including question time are restricted to a maximum length of 30 minutes.</p>
<p>If you wish to make a deputation to a Council meeting, please complete the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/deputation-request-form-corp-frm-516.pdf" target="_self" title="Deputation-Request-Form-CORP-FRM-516" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Deputation Request Form<span class="file-info">(PDF, 189KB)</span></a> and forward to the Chief Executive Officer at <a href="mailto:info@wdrc.qld.gov.au"></a><a href="mailto:records@isaac.qld.gov.au">records@isaac.qld.gov.au</a>, via post to PO Box 97, Moranbah, Qld 4744  or deliver to a Council Customer Service Centre.  Applications must be received not less than seven (7) business days before the meeting unless otherwise determined by the CEO.</p>
<p>Further information on Deputations to Council can be found in the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/standing_orders_and_meeting_procedures_stat_pro_025.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing_Orders_and_Meeting_Procedures_STAT_PRO_025" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="file-info">(PDF, 360KB)</span></a><a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>

        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();

                            <!-- OC Layout Element Conent Template -->
							              <!--normalTemplateStart--><h1 class='oc-page-title '>Council Meetings</h1>

<p>Council holds monthly Ordinary Meetings and Standing Committee Meetings. Minutes from each past meeting are available through the search function below.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">Alternatively, you can view these documents and previous years' minutes by visiting the reception at Council's Moranbah Administration Centre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">T</span>he <em style="color: inherit; font-size: 1em; font-family: inherit;">Local Government Regulation </em><em>2012</em> requires Council to ensure a copy of the minutes of each Council meeting is available for inspection by the public, at a local government's public office and on its website, within 10 days after the end of a meeting; and when the minutes have been confirmed — must be available for purchase at the local government's public office. </p>
<div data-type="0" data-title-level="2" class="oc-wysiwyg-container">
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Attending Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council's Ordinary and Special meetings are open to the public as part of Council's commitment to transparent decision making and engagement with our community.</p>
<p>Ordinary Meetings are held at Isaac's Customer Services Centres on a rotational basis.</p>
<p>Due to the varied sizes of our Council Chambers, the number of public attendees at each meeting is limited. If you wish to attend a council meeting, please arrive early to secure a seat as there is no booking system in place. Once all seating in the chambers is occupied, we are unable to accept additional attendees.</p>
<p>The rules for conducting meetings are dictated by:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-017" target="_blank">Local Government Act 2009</a></em></li>
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2012-0236" target="_blank">Local Government Regulation 2012</a></em></li>
<li><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i> <span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Conduct of Council Meetings Policy<span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a></li>
<li><a href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025_1.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p>Public attendees must not interrupt the conduct of business at council meetings.  If a person interrupts or obstructs the proper conduct of the meeting, the Chairperson of the meeting may ask the person to withdraw from the meeting place.</p>
<p>Recording of council meetings is prohibited unless first approved by the Chairperson of the meeting.</p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Council Meeting Sessions</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The <em>Local Government Regulation 2012</em> allows Council to close meetings to the public in order to discuss particular matters where they consider it necessary.  Council resolutions (decisions) cannot be made while the meeting is closed to the public, the matter can be discussed and the decision made once the meeting is again in open session. </p>
<p>Council meetings may be closed to the public for the following reasons:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the appointment, discipline or dismissal of the Chief Executive Officer</li>
<li>industrial matters affecting employees</li>
<li>the Council’s budget</li>
<li>rating concessions</li>
<li>legal advice obtained by the Council or legal proceedings involving the Council including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the Council</li>
<li>matters that may directly affect the health and safety of an individual or a group of individuals</li>
<li>negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the Council for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the Council</li>
<li>negotiations relating to the taking of land by the Council under the <em>Acquisition of Land Act 1967</em></li>
<li>a matter the Council is required to keep confidential under a law of, or formal arrangement with, the Commonwealth or State</li>
</ul>
<p>When dealing with confidential agenda items, Council will resolve to enter into a closed session which requires all visitors and guests to vacate the Council Chambers until the meeting is again opened by Council resolution.</p>

<h2>Public Participation at Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The community can engage with Council through our meeting processes in the following ways:</p>
<h5>Petitioning Council</h5>
<p>A petition is a formal written request used to lobby a law-making body such as local government. It may request an amendment to general law or the review of an administrative decision. The petition is placed before the law-making body with the object of implementing the particular action or amendment. Petitioning is one of the traditional forms by which people can make requests direct to Council.</p>
<p>Petitions should not be used to request completion of operational works such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>having a water meter repaired</li>
<li>requesting road repairs</li>
</ul>
<h5>Guidelines for Petitions</h5>
<p>All petitions must meet the following requirements to be determined to be a property made petition for consideration by Council:</p>
<ul>
<li>Contain a clear and concise statement identifying the subject matter of the petition and the action sought from Council</li>
<li>Include a statement specifying the range of numbered of pages to the petition and the total number of signatories</li>
<li>Record a brief statement on each page of the subject matter and the action requested</li>
<li>Contain the full printed name, address, phone number and signature of the person lodging the petition, or if acting on behalf of organisation/group, name of organisation/group</li>
<li>List the names, addresses and signatures of those people who support the petition</li>
<li>Be in the English language or accompanied by a translation certified to be a true and correct translation (including contact details of the translator)</li>
<li>Be a standalone document with no letters, affidavits, or other documents attached</li>
<li>Be respectful and not contain any offensive, defamatory, indecent or abusive language or substance or otherwise offend any rule or practice of Council</li>
<li>Be clearly written or printed and be free from erasures or alterations</li>
<li>Meet all stipulations</li>
<li>Not be requests for grants of public money or remission of any duties</li>
</ul>
<p>Petitions that do not meet the criteria listed above will be deemed invalid and will not be received by Council.</p>
<p>This <a href="https://www.isaac.qld.gov.au/downloads/file/3318/petition-to-council-form"></a><a title="Petition_to_Council_Form.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition_to_council_form.pdf" target="_blank" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>sample petition<span class="file-info">(PDF, 57KB)</span></a> may be used as a guide.</p>
<h5>Signing a Petition</h5>
<p>A petition must be signed by a minimum of ten (10) persons aged 18 years or older, clearly stating their name and address. Each person may not sign more than once and each signature must be an original written upon the petition itself and not pasted upon it or otherwise affixed or transferred to it (e.g. scanned, pasted, photocopied, etc.).</p>
<p>Persons signing the petition must only be signing on behalf of themselves and not acting as proxy for another person.</p>
<h5>Addressing and Lodging the Petition</h5>
<p>A person may lodge a petition with the Council by submitting the petition to an Isaac Regional Council Customer Service Centre in person, or by mail addressed to:</p>
<p>Chief Executive Officer<br />
Isaac Regional Council<br />
PO Box 97<br />
Moranbah Qld 4744</p>
<h5>Actioning a Petition</h5>
<p>Once registered the petition will be forwarded to the CEO and the following process will apply.</p>
<p><img alt="Petition Flowchart.JPG" src="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition-flowchart.jpg?w=954&h=593" /></p>
<p>If the petition lodged is not to be tabled, the Council will notify the person lodging the petition within twenty-one (21) days of lodgement, the reasons for it not being tabled.</p>
<p>If the petition is to be tabled, Council will advise the person lodging the petition, the date the petition is to be tabled.</p>
<h5>Deciding a Petition</h5>
<p>Council will decide what action, if any, it will take on the petition after the petition is tabled at its ordinary meeting.</p>
<p>In the minutes of the deciding meeting, Council will record the subject matter of the petition, the number of signatories to the petition, and what action, if any, it will take.</p>
<p>The Council will inform the person who has lodged the petition of Council's decision within twenty-one (21) days of the petition being tabled.</p>
<h5>Petitioning other Levels of Government</h5>
<p>Find out more about petitioning other levels of the Australian government:</p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/e-petitions">Petition to House of Representatives - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Petitions/Senate_Petitions">Petition to Senate - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.parliament.qld.gov.au/Work-of-the-Assembly/Petitions">Petition to Queensland Parliament - State government website</a></p>
<p>Further information on Petitions to Council can be found in the <a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>
<h4>Deputations</h4>
<p>Deputations are where an individual or a small group address Council on issues that are important to them.  The address can be on any topic, it does not need to be in relation to an item on the Meeting agenda.  Deputations from the public are welcome at Council's Ordinary Meetings.  Deputations including question time are restricted to a maximum length of 30 minutes.</p>
<p>If you wish to make a deputation to a Council meeting, please complete the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/deputation-request-form-corp-frm-516.pdf" target="_self" title="Deputation-Request-Form-CORP-FRM-516" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Deputation Request Form<span class="file-info">(PDF, 189KB)</span></a> and forward to the Chief Executive Officer at <a href="mailto:info@wdrc.qld.gov.au"></a><a href="mailto:records@isaac.qld.gov.au">records@isaac.qld.gov.au</a>, via post to PO Box 97, Moranbah, Qld 4744  or deliver to a Council Customer Service Centre.  Applications must be received not less than seven (7) business days before the meeting unless otherwise determined by the CEO.</p>
<p>Further information on Deputations to Council can be found in the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/standing_orders_and_meeting_procedures_stat_pro_025.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing_Orders_and_Meeting_Procedures_STAT_PRO_025" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="file-info">(PDF, 360KB)</span></a><a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>
<p> </p>

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>

                            <!-- OC Layout Element Conent Template -->
							              <!--normalTemplateStart--><h1 class='oc-page-title '>Council Meetings</h1>

<p>Council holds monthly Ordinary Meetings and Standing Committee Meetings. Minutes from each past meeting are available through the search function below.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">Alternatively, you can view these documents and previous years' minutes by visiting the reception at Council's Moranbah Administration Centre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">T</span>he <em style="color: inherit; font-size: 1em; font-family: inherit;">Local Government Regulation </em><em>2012</em> requires Council to ensure a copy of the minutes of each Council meeting is available for inspection by the public, at a local government's public office and on its website, within 10 days after the end of a meeting; and when the minutes have been confirmed — must be available for purchase at the local government's public office. </p>
<div data-type="0" data-title-level="2" class="oc-wysiwyg-container">
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Attending Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council's Ordinary and Special meetings are open to the public as part of Council's commitment to transparent decision making and engagement with our community.</p>
<p>Ordinary Meetings are held at Isaac's Customer Services Centres on a rotational basis.</p>
<p>Due to the varied sizes of our Council Chambers, the number of public attendees at each meeting is limited. If you wish to attend a council meeting, please arrive early to secure a seat as there is no booking system in place. Once all seating in the chambers is occupied, we are unable to accept additional attendees.</p>
<p>The rules for conducting meetings are dictated by:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-017" target="_blank">Local Government Act 2009</a></em></li>
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2012-0236" target="_blank">Local Government Regulation 2012</a></em></li>
<li><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i> <span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Conduct of Council Meetings Policy<span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a></li>
<li><a href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025_1.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p>Public attendees must not interrupt the conduct of business at council meetings.  If a person interrupts or obstructs the proper conduct of the meeting, the Chairperson of the meeting may ask the person to withdraw from the meeting place.</p>
<p>Recording of council meetings is prohibited unless first approved by the Chairperson of the meeting.</p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Council Meeting Sessions</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The <em>Local Government Regulation 2012</em> allows Council to close meetings to the public in order to discuss particular matters where they consider it necessary.  Council resolutions (decisions) cannot be made while the meeting is closed to the public, the matter can be discussed and the decision made once the meeting is again in open session. </p>
<p>Council meetings may be closed to the public for the following reasons:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the appointment, discipline or dismissal of the Chief Executive Officer</li>
<li>industrial matters affecting employees</li>
<li>the Council’s budget</li>
<li>rating concessions</li>
<li>legal advice obtained by the Council or legal proceedings involving the Council including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the Council</li>
<li>matters that may directly affect the health and safety of an individual or a group of individuals</li>
<li>negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the Council for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the Council</li>
<li>negotiations relating to the taking of land by the Council under the <em>Acquisition of Land Act 1967</em></li>
<li>a matter the Council is required to keep confidential under a law of, or formal arrangement with, the Commonwealth or State</li>
</ul>
<p>When dealing with confidential agenda items, Council will resolve to enter into a closed session which requires all visitors and guests to vacate the Council Chambers until the meeting is again opened by Council resolution.</p>

<h2>Public Participation at Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The community can engage with Council through our meeting processes in the following ways:</p>
<h5>Petitioning Council</h5>
<p>A petition is a formal written request used to lobby a law-making body such as local government. It may request an amendment to general law or the review of an administrative decision. The petition is placed before the law-making body with the object of implementing the particular action or amendment. Petitioning is one of the traditional forms by which people can make requests direct to Council.</p>
<p>Petitions should not be used to request completion of operational works such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>having a water meter repaired</li>
<li>requesting road repairs</li>
</ul>
<h5>Guidelines for Petitions</h5>
<p>All petitions must meet the following requirements to be determined to be a property made petition for consideration by Council:</p>
<ul>
<li>Contain a clear and concise statement identifying the subject matter of the petition and the action sought from Council</li>
<li>Include a statement specifying the range of numbered of pages to the petition and the total number of signatories</li>
<li>Record a brief statement on each page of the subject matter and the action requested</li>
<li>Contain the full printed name, address, phone number and signature of the person lodging the petition, or if acting on behalf of organisation/group, name of organisation/group</li>
<li>List the names, addresses and signatures of those people who support the petition</li>
<li>Be in the English language or accompanied by a translation certified to be a true and correct translation (including contact details of the translator)</li>
<li>Be a standalone document with no letters, affidavits, or other documents attached</li>
<li>Be respectful and not contain any offensive, defamatory, indecent or abusive language or substance or otherwise offend any rule or practice of Council</li>
<li>Be clearly written or printed and be free from erasures or alterations</li>
<li>Meet all stipulations</li>
<li>Not be requests for grants of public money or remission of any duties</li>
</ul>
<p>Petitions that do not meet the criteria listed above will be deemed invalid and will not be received by Council.</p>
<p>This <a href="https://www.isaac.qld.gov.au/downloads/file/3318/petition-to-council-form"></a><a title="Petition_to_Council_Form.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition_to_council_form.pdf" target="_blank" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>sample petition<span class="file-info">(PDF, 57KB)</span></a> may be used as a guide.</p>
<h5>Signing a Petition</h5>
<p>A petition must be signed by a minimum of ten (10) persons aged 18 years or older, clearly stating their name and address. Each person may not sign more than once and each signature must be an original written upon the petition itself and not pasted upon it or otherwise affixed or transferred to it (e.g. scanned, pasted, photocopied, etc.).</p>
<p>Persons signing the petition must only be signing on behalf of themselves and not acting as proxy for another person.</p>
<h5>Addressing and Lodging the Petition</h5>
<p>A person may lodge a petition with the Council by submitting the petition to an Isaac Regional Council Customer Service Centre in person, or by mail addressed to:</p>
<p>Chief Executive Officer<br />
Isaac Regional Council<br />
PO Box 97<br />
Moranbah Qld 4744</p>
<h5>Actioning a Petition</h5>
<p>Once registered the petition will be forwarded to the CEO and the following process will apply.</p>
<p><img alt="Petition Flowchart.JPG" src="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition-flowchart.jpg?w=954&h=593" /></p>
<p>If the petition lodged is not to be tabled, the Council will notify the person lodging the petition within twenty-one (21) days of lodgement, the reasons for it not being tabled.</p>
<p>If the petition is to be tabled, Council will advise the person lodging the petition, the date the petition is to be tabled.</p>
<h5>Deciding a Petition</h5>
<p>Council will decide what action, if any, it will take on the petition after the petition is tabled at its ordinary meeting.</p>
<p>In the minutes of the deciding meeting, Council will record the subject matter of the petition, the number of signatories to the petition, and what action, if any, it will take.</p>
<p>The Council will inform the person who has lodged the petition of Council's decision within twenty-one (21) days of the petition being tabled.</p>
<h5>Petitioning other Levels of Government</h5>
<p>Find out more about petitioning other levels of the Australian government:</p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/e-petitions">Petition to House of Representatives - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Petitions/Senate_Petitions">Petition to Senate - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.parliament.qld.gov.au/Work-of-the-Assembly/Petitions">Petition to Queensland Parliament - State government website</a></p>
<p>Further information on Petitions to Council can be found in the <a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>
<h4>Deputations</h4>
<p>Deputations are where an individual or a small group address Council on issues that are important to them.  The address can be on any topic, it does not need to be in relation to an item on the Meeting agenda.  Deputations from the public are welcome at Council's Ordinary Meetings.  Deputations including question time are restricted to a maximum length of 30 minutes.</p>
<p>If you wish to make a deputation to a Council meeting, please complete the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/deputation-request-form-corp-frm-516.pdf" target="_self" title="Deputation-Request-Form-CORP-FRM-516" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Deputation Request Form<span class="file-info">(PDF, 189KB)</span></a> and forward to the Chief Executive Officer at <a href="mailto:info@wdrc.qld.gov.au"></a><a href="mailto:records@isaac.qld.gov.au">records@isaac.qld.gov.au</a>, via post to PO Box 97, Moranbah, Qld 4744  or deliver to a Council Customer Service Centre.  Applications must be received not less than seven (7) business days before the meeting unless otherwise determined by the CEO.</p>
<p>Further information on Deputations to Council can be found in the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/standing_orders_and_meeting_procedures_stat_pro_025.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing_Orders_and_Meeting_Procedures_STAT_PRO_025" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="file-info">(PDF, 360KB)</span></a><a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>

							              <!--normalTemplateStart--><h1 class='oc-page-title '>Council Meetings</h1>

<p>Council holds monthly Ordinary Meetings and Standing Committee Meetings. Minutes from each past meeting are available through the search function below.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">Alternatively, you can view these documents and previous years' minutes by visiting the reception at Council's Moranbah Administration Centre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">T</span>he <em style="color: inherit; font-size: 1em; font-family: inherit;">Local Government Regulation </em><em>2012</em> requires Council to ensure a copy of the minutes of each Council meeting is available for inspection by the public, at a local government's public office and on its website, within 10 days after the end of a meeting; and when the minutes have been confirmed — must be available for purchase at the local government's public office. </p>
<div data-type="0" data-title-level="2" class="oc-wysiwyg-container">
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Attending Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council's Ordinary and Special meetings are open to the public as part of Council's commitment to transparent decision making and engagement with our community.</p>
<p>Ordinary Meetings are held at Isaac's Customer Services Centres on a rotational basis.</p>
<p>Due to the varied sizes of our Council Chambers, the number of public attendees at each meeting is limited. If you wish to attend a council meeting, please arrive early to secure a seat as there is no booking system in place. Once all seating in the chambers is occupied, we are unable to accept additional attendees.</p>
<p>The rules for conducting meetings are dictated by:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-017" target="_blank">Local Government Act 2009</a></em></li>
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2012-0236" target="_blank">Local Government Regulation 2012</a></em></li>
<li><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i> <span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Conduct of Council Meetings Policy<span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a></li>
<li><a href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025_1.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p>Public attendees must not interrupt the conduct of business at council meetings.  If a person interrupts or obstructs the proper conduct of the meeting, the Chairperson of the meeting may ask the person to withdraw from the meeting place.</p>
<p>Recording of council meetings is prohibited unless first approved by the Chairperson of the meeting.</p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Council Meeting Sessions</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The <em>Local Government Regulation 2012</em> allows Council to close meetings to the public in order to discuss particular matters where they consider it necessary.  Council resolutions (decisions) cannot be made while the meeting is closed to the public, the matter can be discussed and the decision made once the meeting is again in open session. </p>
<p>Council meetings may be closed to the public for the following reasons:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the appointment, discipline or dismissal of the Chief Executive Officer</li>
<li>industrial matters affecting employees</li>
<li>the Council’s budget</li>
<li>rating concessions</li>
<li>legal advice obtained by the Council or legal proceedings involving the Council including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the Council</li>
<li>matters that may directly affect the health and safety of an individual or a group of individuals</li>
<li>negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the Council for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the Council</li>
<li>negotiations relating to the taking of land by the Council under the <em>Acquisition of Land Act 1967</em></li>
<li>a matter the Council is required to keep confidential under a law of, or formal arrangement with, the Commonwealth or State</li>
</ul>
<p>When dealing with confidential agenda items, Council will resolve to enter into a closed session which requires all visitors and guests to vacate the Council Chambers until the meeting is again opened by Council resolution.</p>

<h2>Public Participation at Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The community can engage with Council through our meeting processes in the following ways:</p>
<h5>Petitioning Council</h5>
<p>A petition is a formal written request used to lobby a law-making body such as local government. It may request an amendment to general law or the review of an administrative decision. The petition is placed before the law-making body with the object of implementing the particular action or amendment. Petitioning is one of the traditional forms by which people can make requests direct to Council.</p>
<p>Petitions should not be used to request completion of operational works such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>having a water meter repaired</li>
<li>requesting road repairs</li>
</ul>
<h5>Guidelines for Petitions</h5>
<p>All petitions must meet the following requirements to be determined to be a property made petition for consideration by Council:</p>
<ul>
<li>Contain a clear and concise statement identifying the subject matter of the petition and the action sought from Council</li>
<li>Include a statement specifying the range of numbered of pages to the petition and the total number of signatories</li>
<li>Record a brief statement on each page of the subject matter and the action requested</li>
<li>Contain the full printed name, address, phone number and signature of the person lodging the petition, or if acting on behalf of organisation/group, name of organisation/group</li>
<li>List the names, addresses and signatures of those people who support the petition</li>
<li>Be in the English language or accompanied by a translation certified to be a true and correct translation (including contact details of the translator)</li>
<li>Be a standalone document with no letters, affidavits, or other documents attached</li>
<li>Be respectful and not contain any offensive, defamatory, indecent or abusive language or substance or otherwise offend any rule or practice of Council</li>
<li>Be clearly written or printed and be free from erasures or alterations</li>
<li>Meet all stipulations</li>
<li>Not be requests for grants of public money or remission of any duties</li>
</ul>
<p>Petitions that do not meet the criteria listed above will be deemed invalid and will not be received by Council.</p>
<p>This <a href="https://www.isaac.qld.gov.au/downloads/file/3318/petition-to-council-form"></a><a title="Petition_to_Council_Form.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition_to_council_form.pdf" target="_blank" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>sample petition<span class="file-info">(PDF, 57KB)</span></a> may be used as a guide.</p>
<h5>Signing a Petition</h5>
<p>A petition must be signed by a minimum of ten (10) persons aged 18 years or older, clearly stating their name and address. Each person may not sign more than once and each signature must be an original written upon the petition itself and not pasted upon it or otherwise affixed or transferred to it (e.g. scanned, pasted, photocopied, etc.).</p>
<p>Persons signing the petition must only be signing on behalf of themselves and not acting as proxy for another person.</p>
<h5>Addressing and Lodging the Petition</h5>
<p>A person may lodge a petition with the Council by submitting the petition to an Isaac Regional Council Customer Service Centre in person, or by mail addressed to:</p>
<p>Chief Executive Officer<br />
Isaac Regional Council<br />
PO Box 97<br />
Moranbah Qld 4744</p>
<h5>Actioning a Petition</h5>
<p>Once registered the petition will be forwarded to the CEO and the following process will apply.</p>
<p><img alt="Petition Flowchart.JPG" src="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/corporate-information/accessing-council-information/petition-flowchart.jpg?w=954&h=593" /></p>
<p>If the petition lodged is not to be tabled, the Council will notify the person lodging the petition within twenty-one (21) days of lodgement, the reasons for it not being tabled.</p>
<p>If the petition is to be tabled, Council will advise the person lodging the petition, the date the petition is to be tabled.</p>
<h5>Deciding a Petition</h5>
<p>Council will decide what action, if any, it will take on the petition after the petition is tabled at its ordinary meeting.</p>
<p>In the minutes of the deciding meeting, Council will record the subject matter of the petition, the number of signatories to the petition, and what action, if any, it will take.</p>
<p>The Council will inform the person who has lodged the petition of Council's decision within twenty-one (21) days of the petition being tabled.</p>
<h5>Petitioning other Levels of Government</h5>
<p>Find out more about petitioning other levels of the Australian government:</p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/e-petitions">Petition to House of Representatives - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Petitions/Senate_Petitions">Petition to Senate - Federal government website</a></p>
<p><a href="https://www.parliament.qld.gov.au/Work-of-the-Assembly/Petitions">Petition to Queensland Parliament - State government website</a></p>
<p>Further information on Petitions to Council can be found in the <a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>
<h4>Deputations</h4>
<p>Deputations are where an individual or a small group address Council on issues that are important to them.  The address can be on any topic, it does not need to be in relation to an item on the Meeting agenda.  Deputations from the public are welcome at Council's Ordinary Meetings.  Deputations including question time are restricted to a maximum length of 30 minutes.</p>
<p>If you wish to make a deputation to a Council meeting, please complete the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/deputation-request-form-corp-frm-516.pdf" target="_self" title="Deputation-Request-Form-CORP-FRM-516" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Deputation Request Form<span class="file-info">(PDF, 189KB)</span></a> and forward to the Chief Executive Officer at <a href="mailto:info@wdrc.qld.gov.au"></a><a href="mailto:records@isaac.qld.gov.au">records@isaac.qld.gov.au</a>, via post to PO Box 97, Moranbah, Qld 4744  or deliver to a Council Customer Service Centre.  Applications must be received not less than seven (7) business days before the meeting unless otherwise determined by the CEO.</p>
<p>Further information on Deputations to Council can be found in the <a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/standing_orders_and_meeting_procedures_stat_pro_025.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing_Orders_and_Meeting_Procedures_STAT_PRO_025" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><span class="file-info">(PDF, 360KB)</span></a><a title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures.<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></p>

    <script>
        // OCNOW-11988 (Cursor): Proactively focus skip link when returning from browser chrome.
        // Must run inline (not deferred oc_main.js) so focus is intercepted before NVDA speaks footer.
        (function () {
            var awaitingReentry = false;
            var inertSupported = 'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype;

            function isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(node) {
                return node != null && !document.documentElement.contains(node);
            }

            function getSkipContainer() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-container');
            }

            function getSkipLink() {
                return document.getElementById('skip-to-content-link');
            }

            function applyGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = true;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    if (children[i] !== skipContainer) {
                        children[i].setAttribute('inert', '');
                    }
                }
            }

            function clearGuard() {
                awaitingReentry = false;
                if (!inertSupported) {
                    return;
                }
                var children = document.body.children;
                for (var i = 0; i < children.length; i++) {
                    children[i].removeAttribute('inert');
                }
            }

            function isSkipLinkElement(target) {
                if (!target) {
                    return false;
                }
                var skipContainer = getSkipContainer();
                return target.id === 'skip-to-content-link' ||
                    (skipContainer && skipContainer.contains(target));
            }

            function focusSkipLink() {
                var skipLink = getSkipLink();
                if (!skipLink) {
                    return;
                }
                if (window.scrollY > 0) {
                    window.scrollTo(0, 0);
                }
                skipLink.focus({ preventScroll: true });
            }

            function scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus() {
                window.setTimeout(function () {
                    if (!document.hasFocus()) {
                        applyGuard();
                    }
                }, 0);
            }

            document.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
                if (isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget)) {
                    applyGuard();
                }
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
                if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                } else if (e.key === 'F6' || (e.key === 'l' && e.ctrlKey)) {
                    scheduleGuardIfDocumentLostFocus();
                }
            }, true);

            window.addEventListener('focus', function () {
                if (!awaitingReentry) {
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
            }, true);

            document.addEventListener('focusin', function (e) {
                var reentryFromChrome = awaitingReentry || isExplicitlyOutsideDocument(e.relatedTarget);
                if (!reentryFromChrome) {
                    return;
                }
                if (isSkipLinkElement(e.target)) {
                    clearGuard();
                    return;
                }
                applyGuard();
                focusSkipLink();
                clearGuard();
            }, true);
        })();
    </script>

                            <!-- OC Layout Element Conent Template -->
							              <!--normalTemplateStart--><h1 class='oc-page-title '>Council Meetings</h1>

<p>Council holds monthly Ordinary Meetings and Standing Committee Meetings. Minutes from each past meeting are available through the search function below.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">Alternatively, you can view these documents and previous years' minutes by visiting the reception at Council's Moranbah Administration Centre.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">T</span>he <em style="color: inherit; font-size: 1em; font-family: inherit;">Local Government Regulation </em><em>2012</em> requires Council to ensure a copy of the minutes of each Council meeting is available for inspection by the public, at a local government's public office and on its website, within 10 days after the end of a meeting; and when the minutes have been confirmed — must be available for purchase at the local government's public office. </p>
<div data-type="0" data-title-level="2" class="oc-wysiwyg-container">
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Attending Council Meetings</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council's Ordinary and Special meetings are open to the public as part of Council's commitment to transparent decision making and engagement with our community.</p>
<p>Ordinary Meetings are held at Isaac's Customer Services Centres on a rotational basis.</p>
<p>Due to the varied sizes of our Council Chambers, the number of public attendees at each meeting is limited. If you wish to attend a council meeting, please arrive early to secure a seat as there is no booking system in place. Once all seating in the chambers is occupied, we are unable to accept additional attendees.</p>
<p>The rules for conducting meetings are dictated by:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/act-2009-017" target="_blank">Local Government Act 2009</a></em></li>
<li>the <em><a href="https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/html/inforce/current/sl-2012-0236" target="_blank">Local Government Regulation 2012</a></em></li>
<li><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i> <span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a><a href="/files/assets/public/v/1/your-council/council-meetings/conduct-of-council-meetings-policy-v4-stat-pol-043.pdf" target="_self" title="Conduct-of-Council-Meetings-Policy-v4-STAT-POL-043" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Conduct of Council Meetings Policy<span class="file-info">(PDF, 391KB)</span></a></li>
<li><a href="/files/content/public/v/67/your-council/council-meetings/standing-orders-and-meeting-procedures-stat-pro-025_1.pdf" target="_self" title="Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures (STAT-PRO-025).pdf" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Standing Orders and Meeting Procedures<span class="file-info">(PDF, 523KB)</span></a></li>
</ul>
<p>Public attendees must not interrupt the conduct of business at council meetings.  If a person interrupts or obstructs the proper conduct of the meeting, the Chairperson of the meeting may ask the person to withdraw from the meeting place.</p>
<p>Recording of council meetings is prohibited unless first approved by the Chairperson of the meeting.</p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel">
<h2>Council Meeting Sessions</h2>
<div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The <em>Local Government Regulation 2012</em> allows Council to close meetings to the public in order to discuss particular matters where they consider it necessary.  Council resolutions (decisions) cannot be made while the meeting is closed to the public, the matter can be discussed and the decision made once the meeting is again in open session. </p>
<p>Council meetings may be closed to the public for the following reasons:</p>
<ul type="disc">
<li>the appointment, discipline or dismissal of the Chief Executive Officer</li>
<li>industrial matters affecting employees</li>
<li>the Council’s budget</li>
<li>rating concessions</li>
<li>legal advice obtained by the Council or legal proceedings involving the Council including, for example, legal proceedings that may be taken by or against the Council</li>
<li>matters that may directly affect the health and safety of an individual or a group of individuals</li>
<li>negotiations relating to a commercial matter involving the Council for which a public discussion would be likely to prejudice the interests of the Council</li>
<li>negotiations relating to the taking of land by the Council under the <em>Acquisition of Land Act 1967</em></li>
<li>a matter the Council is required to keep confidential under a law of, or formal arrangement with, the Commonwealth or State</li>
</ul>
<p>When dealing with confidential agenda items, Council will resolve to enter into a closed session which requires all visitors and guests to vacate the Council Chambers until the meeting is again opened by Council resolution.</p>
